hints.title: Combinatorial Contribution Modeling
hints.text: Model the contribution of each digit as binomial coefficients modulo 10.

hints.title: Decomposition by Prime Moduli
hints.text: For a string of length n, the final two digits are formed by linear combinations weighted by binom(n - 2, i).

hints.title: Chinese Remainder Reconstruction
hints.text: Compute binomial coefficients modulo 2 and modulo 5 separately using Lucas theorem, then combine them via Chinese remainder theorem.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def hasSameDigits(self, s: str) -> bool:
        n = len(s)
        m = n - 2
        lookup = [[0, 6, 2, 8, 4], [5, 1, 7, 3, 9]]

        def lucas(n_val: int, k_val: int, p: int) -> int:
            res = 1
            while n_val > 0 or k_val > 0:
                ni, ki = n_val % p, k_val % p
                if ni < ki:
                    return 0
                comb = 1
                for i in range(ki):
                    comb = comb * (ni - i) // (i + 1)
                res = (res * (comb % p)) % p
                n_val //= p
                k_val //= p
            return res

        def nck_mod_10(n_val: int, k_val: int) -> int:
            m2 = lucas(n_val, k_val, 2)
            m5 = lucas(n_val, k_val, 5)
            return lookup[m2][m5]

        num1 = 0
        num2 = 0
        for i in range(m + 1):
            c = nck_mod_10(m, i)
            num1 = (num1 + c * int(s[i])) % 10
            num2 = (num2 + c * int(s[i + 1])) % 10
        return num1 == num2
```

complexity.notes: Evaluates Lucas theorem for prime moduli 2 and 5 to compute binomial coefficients modulo 10.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: O(n^2) simulation times out because n can reach 10^5.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Decomposing modulo 10 into prime moduli 2 and 5 allows O(log n) coefficient evaluation.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Recognize Pascal triangle coefficients modulo composite base 10 and apply Lucas theorem.
